newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends sharply weaker but off lows.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends sharply weaker but off lows.

text.p: Speculative liquidation drove CSCE world sugar futures sharply weaker in early trade, but prices managed to climb off the lows to settle toward the middle of the day's range, a bullish signal for Monday's market, industry sources said.
They blamed weakness in the October contract on today's options expiry. The bulk of options activity centered around the strike price of 11.50, today's low.

"It's all technical trade now," said Jim Cordier, an analyst with Allendale Commodities. He said prices are trading within a channel supported at 11.35 and capped at 11.75, the high made September 3, basis the March contract.
Prices are likely to trade sideways and then work higher, over the next two weeks, he said.

One dealer called today's close "a constructive sign." While follow-through selling is possible Monday, enough speculative postions were taken out today to hold spot October above support at 11.50, he said, noting today's hefty volume of 48,879 lots.
The October contract settled 0.25 weaker at 11.64, having ranged from 11.84 to 11.50. March eased 0.22 to end at 11.45, while the back months finished the day 0.21 to 0.16 weaker.
Resistance was pegged in the mid 11.80-cent per lb range in October, and at 11.58 in March.
The October/March spread closed at 0.19, compared with 0.22 at Thursday's close.

Some market sources said A U.S. Department of Agriculture report released Thursday contributed to the market's weakness, while others said the data were expected. The USDA report pegged world sugar output at 121.4 million tonnes, up from a May estimate of 120.2 million tonnes. Production estimates for India and Brazil, were also raised.
LCE white sugar futures finished sharply lower as the spot October contract expired. The contract went out at $339.00, off $7.30, while December finished $4.40 lower at $338.50.
